questions.q: Where does Fabric's lineage view come from, and what setup does it require?
options: Every workspace has one automatically, with no extra setup or licensing
It must be manually enabled per workspace by an admin
It only exists after you connect a dataflow to a semantic model
It requires a separate Purview subscription to activate
questions.explain: Every workspace automatically has a lineage view — it's built in, not something you turn on.

questions.q: In the lineage diagram, what does an arrow from Card A to Card B mean?
options: Data flows from A into B — A is upstream of B
Card A was created before Card B
Card A and Card B share the same owner
Card B has a higher sensitivity label than Card A
questions.explain: Arrows show the direction of data flow: the source item is upstream, the item it feeds is downstream.

questions.q: What does lineage view show about items downstream of the current item that live in a different workspace?
options: It doesn't show them — that's what impact analysis is for
It shows them in a greyed-out section at the bottom
It shows them, but without refresh timestamps
It merges them into the current workspace's diagram automatically
questions.explain: Lineage view renders one workspace's graph plus external upstream sources one step back. Downstream items in other workspaces aren't shown there — exploring them is impact analysis's job.

questions.q: What does a warning triangle next to a card's refresh timestamp in lineage view indicate?
options: The item's last refresh failed or needs attention
The item has not been shared with anyone yet
The item is scheduled for deletion
The item contains personally identifiable information
questions.explain: Refresh status is shown directly on the card: a plain timestamp means the refresh completed, while a warning triangle flags a problem — exactly where to look first if a downstream report looks stale.

questions.q: Which workspace role can open a workspace's lineage view but will NOT see its data source cards?
options: Viewer
Admin
Member
Contributor
questions.explain: Any user with a role in the workspace can access lineage view, but users with the Viewer role specifically don't see data source cards — a deliberate governance boundary.
